comparator.name: English Language and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026 entrant programme has a 120 EC major and 60 EC elective profile. The major includes eight core courses, a 30 EC specialisation, its 7.5 EC context course, a 7.5 EC methodology choice, a 7.5 EC Thesis Lab and a 7.5 EC thesis. This example uses The Social Life of English with its associated Topics in Linguistics and the first listed methodology choice, Methods and Statistics 1. The 60 EC profile includes a 30 EC package and 30 EC of further electives. Passing the 0 EC Basic Grammar Test is compulsory.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: English-language literature across periods, cultures and forms
English language, its structures, histories and global varieties
The relationship between language, literature, culture, history and identity
Close reading, writing, literary interpretation and textual transformation
Language acquisition, psycholinguistics and language teaching
Humanities and social-science methods, Thesis Lab and independent bachelor research
adjacent: Literature, media, adaptation and creative transformation
Global English, social variation, identity and belonging
Celtic languages, literatures and medieval textual cultures
questions: How do literary texts shape ideas about individuals and communities?
How does English change across historical periods, regions, social classes and global communities?
How do children and adults acquire additional languages, and how can English be taught?

candidates.label: Language learning and teaching across the lifespan
candidates.reason: Psycholinguistics includes acquisition and bilingualism, and Rhetoric in Action includes coaching children in public speaking. Lifespan psychology offers a broader developmental perspective. Together these do not establish a sequence in acquiring and teaching additional languages.

candidates.label: Celtic literatures and linguistics
candidates.reason: World Myth & Literature provides cross-cultural study of texts and traditions. UCR has no sustained sequence in Celtic languages, medieval Celtic textual traditions or historical grammar.

routeSelection.basis: The general degree target spans language, literature and culture. The first-year core supplies literature and language foundations, while this specialisation connects language history, social variation, identity and English around the world. It is selected for its coverage of the degree’s academic identity independently of the UCR options.

selection.assessment: The closest option combines literature, stylistics, psycholinguistics and cultural research. The two further options add different sequences in adaptation and media production, and in social theory and cultural representation. The additional-language teaching and Celtic directions lack sustained course coverage.

alternatives.label: Literature, Language and Culture
alternatives.labelReason: Literary interpretation, stylistics and psycholinguistics combine with rhetoric, cultural history and research.
alternatives.concept: Study how literary and cultural forms make meaning across periods and communities. Combine close reading, film adaptation, stylistics and psycholinguistics with rhetoric and historical research.
progression: Literary studies and rhetoric prepare students for adaptation, literary theory and applied rhetoric. Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics. Research methods precede advanced historical inquiry.

alternatives.label: Literature, Adaptation and Media
alternatives.labelReason: Literary interpretation connects with film adaptation, documentary, art and creative practice.
alternatives.concept: Study what changes when stories move between books, film and other media. Develop close reading, film analysis and creative practice alongside documentary and art-historical research.
alternatives.distinctness: Adds media archaeology, art history and documentary research and production. These courses support a sustained focus on how stories and images change across forms.
progression: Introductory literature, film and art history prepare students for adaptation, documentary and advanced interpretation. Research design precedes independent literary and visual research.

alternatives.label: Language, Identity and Cultural Representation
alternatives.labelReason: Stylistics and psycholinguistics complement sociology, cultural history and media representation.
alternatives.concept: Explore how people express identity and belonging through language, life writing and media. Use sociology, qualitative research and Indigenous histories to study representation and cultural power.
alternatives.distinctness: Adds comparative politics, modern and contemporary social theory, Indigenous history and environmental media. These courses give the study of identity and representation greater social and historical depth.
progression: Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics. Sociology and qualitative methods support later social theory and research. Media and historical foundations prepare students for advanced work on race and Indigenous histories.

blocks: Utrecht studies English Renaissance literature as a dedicated period. UCR Introduction to Literary Studies teaches close reading across genres and periods.
Both connect texts to historical and cultural change. UCR studies a wider world canon, with works beyond the English-language period studied at Utrecht.
Utrecht studies English-language literature from 1850 to 1950 in a dedicated course. UCR studies modernist narration and subjectivity within its broader literature courses.
UCR embeds research preparation across methods and advanced courses rather than providing a directly equivalent dedicated Thesis Lab.
Utrecht teaches phonetic transcription and pronunciation. UCR Psycholinguistics examines how speech is processed and produced.
Both develop argument and attention to the audience. Utrecht emphasises writing and revision, while UCR studies rhetoric in written and spoken discourse.
Both examine grammar and language choices. UCR uses morphology, syntax and register to explain stylistic effects.
Utrecht studies the historical development of languages in the British Isles. UCR Psycholinguistics studies language processing and acquisition.
UCR offers linguistics, stylistics and psycholinguistics contributions but no dedicated morphosyntax course.
Utrecht studies Old English in its early medieval setting. UCR offers cross-cultural textual interpretation and broader historical study.
UCR studies identity and language across communication, sociology and media rather than in one dedicated course.
UCR offers social and communication analysis but no full sociolinguistics-of-Englishes course.
UCR provides global cultural and communication perspectives but no dedicated World Englishes course.
The selected Utrecht specialisation requires Topics in Linguistics. UCR covers stylistics and psycholinguistics in separate courses.
Both develop empirical research design and statistical analysis. The UCR course also introduces qualitative and experimental approaches.
This is genuine elective/profile space and is preserved without inventing content.
Utrecht requires an individual thesis in English Language and Culture. UCR offers optional independent research alongside advanced course projects.

notes.text: Utrecht requires a sequence in English sound, grammar and language history, followed by a specialisation and an individual thesis. The UCR options combine literary study with broader work in media, language, history and culture.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht studies English-language literature, language and cultures across periods and regions. Students complete a common core, choose a specialisation and write an individual thesis. This example follows The Social Life of English.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines literary interpretation with language, rhetoric and culture. Two further options focus on adaptation and media, or language and cultural representation. Utrecht gives more space to English phonetics, grammar, language history and global varieties of English.

curriculum.limitation: Students must pass the Basic Grammar Test, which carries no credits. The elective profile includes a 30 EC package and 30 EC of further electives, with at least 15 EC at intermediate level.

cellNotes.text: This is the context course for The Social Life of English.
One of four methodology courses. This example follows the first listed option.
Choose a minor, study abroad or a second specialisation. Study abroad, external minors and exceptional combinations require prior approval.
Complete at least three advanced specialisation courses (22.5 EC) before Thesis Lab. The lab assesses a portfolio and research proposal.
Complete Thesis Lab before writing the individual thesis under supervision. Two lecturers assess the thesis.
